title: user
description: One learner account, plus the scheduler settings that are one-to-one with it. RUNTIME class: minted per learner, never committed to this repo — see design/user_state.md §12. Holds no email, no password, no password hash, no IP and no third-party identifier; `user_id` is opaque and `display_name` is learner-set prose, not an identity. Authentication lives outside this contract and owner decision D8 decides where.

x-yomineko.note: The scheduler block is deliberately NOT a separate entity (research/reports/readiness/srs_fsrs.md §5 sketched a USER_SCHEDULER row): it is one-to-one with the account and read on every queue build.

user_id.description: The opaque account address, `usr:<opaque>`. The only identifier that appears anywhere else in the runtime model. No colon inside the opaque part — every card_id is parsed by splitting on ':' (design/user_state.md §2).

locale.description: Interface language. pt-BR is the only locale authored today, and that is a content fact, not a structural one (design/i18n.md).

timezone.description: IANA time-zone name, e.g. `America/Sao_Paulo`. The daily queue rolls over on the learner's LOCAL day, not on UTC, so this is scheduler input and not a display preference.

display_name.description: Learner-set. Not an identity and never used as a key.

entitlement.description: What the account is allowed to reach. The corpus is private paid content, so this gates content, not chrome. Vocabulary owner: design — design/user_state.md#4-user. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

scheduler.description: FSRS-6 settings. Defaults come from design/unlock_enums.json#_deck_defaults, which is the authority for the retention band and the new-card cap.

fsrs_version.description: Which algorithm this account is scheduled by. FSRS-6 -> FSRS-7 is a replay of review_log, not a migration (design/user_state.md §3). Vocabulary owner: design — design/user_state.md#3-what-fsrs-6-actually-needs-and-why-card-is-a-cache. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

desired_retention.description: Target recall probability. Band from design/unlock_enums.json#_deck_defaults.retention_band. The 0.70-0.97 band proposed in research/reports/readiness/srs_fsrs.md §5 is REJECTED: the same defaults block calls >0.97 discouraged, and a band should not reach a value its own defaults warn against (design/user_state.md §10.2).

params.description: The learner's optimized FSRS-6 weight vector, 21 numbers. Null means ship defaults. Trained OFFLINE, monthly, once the account has roughly 400 reviews — never at request time.

reviews_at_training.description: How many review_log rows produced `params`. A weight vector with no sample size behind it cannot be audited, and 21 parameters fitted on 40 reviews is noise.

daily_new_cap.description: New cards admitted per day. Default 10 from design/unlock_enums.json#_deck_defaults.new_per_day. design/srs_design.md §1 said 15; the two prose sources conflicted and unlock_enums.json wins because it is the file the loader and the validators already import (design/user_state.md §10.1).

daily_review_cap.description: Reviews admitted per day. Overflow spills to tomorrow; FSRS handles late reviews natively through its stability/retrievability math.

session.description: Daily-queue budget (design/srs_design.md §3): memory cards fill up to 80% of the budget, skill exercises take the remainder.
